messages.subject: reduce performance issue
parts:
Hello,

I went into a huge performance issue in the reducer that I will do my best to explain here.

I have a dataset with 27659536 rows and 2 columns resident in memory.
Using the data structure defined in my.to.dfs.2, the dataset become stored in HDFS occupying 1,6 GB.

my.to.dfs.2 <- function (object, output = dfs.tempfile(), format = "native") 
   to.dfs(lapply(1:nrow(object), function(i) keyval(NULL, rbind(c(i,Inf,( object[i,]))))), output = dfs.tempfile(), format = "native")

After uploding to HDFS I deleted the dataset from the memory and the environment become with few KB. 
I run the function first.sample.MR with argument the HDFS file. 

    first.sample.MR <- function (X) 
mapreduce(input = X, map = to.map(identity), reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, my.first.sample(vv)))
 
    my.first.sample <- function(x) {
temp <- do.call(rbind,x) 
temp_sample<-sample(temp[,1],1)
return(temp[temp_sample,c(-1,-2)])
    }

The reducer took 42 min, while the same implementation in memory took less than 5 min.

messages.subject: Re: reduce performance issue
parts:
• You are using Hadoop for 1.2 Gb of data. Wrong tool. There are applications of Hadoop to small data, like the computation of an approximation of Pi, but those are not the typical cases and require special tuning and techniques and make sense for huge clusters. 
  • You are comparing memory and disk and complaining that the latter is slower. Know your hardware basics first. Read this paper: http://queue.acm.org/detail.cfm?id=1563874 . A half hour pleasant read will give you the basic numbers.
  • You are using a single reducer because your only key is NULL. That means even if your cluster has 1000 machines (a detail that I didn't find in your message) and is properly configured (you apparently have no system analysis to report, like how many processes are running on how many nodes), you are using a single one. So all this work to use hadoop just to compute at disk rather than memory speed. Get your mapreduce basics first.
  • Rather than posting hundreds of redundant lines of console output, if you are comparing two programs, post  both programs. It could be that your first program is so optimized that I could have learned something. 
  • my.first.sample is defined after you use it in mapreduce. So I don't know what is actually called there. Please make code snippets executable.
  • dfs.tempfile is not exported. Why are you using it without documentation?
Antonio

I went into a huge performance issue in the reducer that I will do my best to explain here.

I have a dataset with 27659536 rows and 2 columns resident in memory.
Using the data structure defined in my.to.dfs.2, the dataset become stored in HDFS occupying 1,6 GB.

my.to.dfs.2 <- function (object, output = dfs.tempfile(), format = "native")

I run the function first.sample.MR with argument the HDFS file. 

    first.sample.MR <- function (X) 
mapreduce(input = X, map = to.map(identity), reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, my.first.sample(vv)))
 
    my.first.sample <- function(x) {
temp <- do.call(rbind,x) 
temp_sample<-sample(temp[,1],1)
return(temp[temp_sample,c(-1,-2)])
